text: Each owner loads its own rows: S4 rwb-litigation loads legal_action into rwb_litigation, P6 rwb-comms loads notice into rwb_comms and S9 rwb-partner loads partner_instruction into rwb_partner, each on its own Flyway sequence, while P1 reads the dump once and hands the packages over and holds no INSERT against another schema.
why: The Ownership Map gives the three tables to S4, P6 and S9 while the legacy story migrates them in the single recovery schema, and DP-01 with DP-15 forbids the cross-schema write the legacy shape would need.
read: Ownership Map legal_action (S4), notice (P6), partner_instruction (S9); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15
confirm: Solution architect at the cut-over rehearsal
impact: A wrong reading would put a cross-schema write in P1 and fail the boundary test; the lawful alternative is three owner loads on three sequences.

text: The extract leaves as one handover package per owner per cut-over business date, written to the cut-over record of the release pipeline and not to a table; the package layout, its file format, the dump's name and layout, and the point where the pipeline writes a package are agreed at the cut-over rehearsal and are not fixed here.
why: No source gives a package or dump shape, and the legacy key names only a cutover step run by the recovery service identity with its breaks on the reconciliation extract.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 Endpoints and AC1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 (one-off bulk work through service APIs)
confirm: Solution architect and data steward at the cut-over rehearsal
impact: A package format change is a rehearsal decision and changes no criterion.

text: The partner instruction is handed over in two slices: this story carries the instruction raised for a legal action with the instruction id, the case, the firm, the instruction type, the instructed_at and the due_at, and RWB-P1-DM008-APP carries the panel performance facts of the same instruction; S9 loads both packages, idempotent on the instruction id.
why: partner_instruction appears in the data table of both RWB-DM-007 and RWB-DM-008, the table has one owner, and the two migrations must not duplicate the row.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 Data table partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and AC1; legacy RWB-DM-008 story; Ownership Map partner_instruction (S9); FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP07 and DP08 rows
confirm: Data steward and the rwb-partner owner
impact: A wrong split would leave a firm with a due date and no performance record, or a performance record with no clock.

text: Ten clean days are counted from the reconciliation_result rows JOB-04 writes for the migrated records, one set per business date: a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan extends the count, and a BREAK row or a new orphan resets it to zero and names the day.
why: AC3 states the outcome only and no source gives the count its rows, its reset rule or its threshold; reconciliation_result is the only record of a clean day the service owns.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 and A2.11.3.1; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result with result PASS or BREAK; DL25
impact: A reset-on-break rule is stricter than a checklist and is the evidence the steward signs; a different rule would let a sign-off stand after a break.

text: The cut-over record of the release pipeline holds the extract definition, the three owner packages, the ten day rows and the data steward's sign-off, and the release pipeline runs the cut-over as one-off bulk work through the service's own operations (API-P1-002, API-P1-003 and API-P1-010), never reading or writing a rwb_* schema.
why: AC3 requires a sign-off and a read-only window without naming a store, and Architecture v5 slide 32 puts one-off bulk work on service APIs and not on schemas.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 and its notes; legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.2 for API-P1-002, API-P1-003 and API-P1-010
impact: A record kept elsewhere would need a store and a retention rule and would add a table this story does not own.

text: The read-only window on the legacy Workbench tables is opened by a grant change the ACE team executes on the legacy schema, and the length of the window is read from the retention rule in force (RWB-P1-E1017-APP); this service only proves the refusal and records the window and its end date.
why: The legacy tables are outside rwb_source_data and no source gives the number of days or the identity that may change their grants.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3 ('the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period'); FSD P1 v3 A2.17; RWB-P1-E1017-APP
confirm: ACE team and the platform administrator
impact: A wrong owner would ask P1 to change another schema; the read-only proof stays with this story either way.

text: Legacy AC1 Extract the Workbench records and AC2 Reconcile the business keys sit with RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG, so this P1 slice claims AC3 only, keeps TC-DM-007-03 and TC-DM-007-04, and leaves TC-DM-007-01 and TC-DM-007-02 with the integration story as the -ITG copies.
why: The split of the key gives AC1 and AC2 to RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG and AC3 to this story, and the integration story already carries the extract rule and the key resolution its criteria test.
read: The split of RWB-DM-007 with acs AC3 for RWB-P1-DM007-APP and AC1, AC2 for RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG; RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG sections 7 and 16
impact: None on the build; a reader looking for the extraction rule finds it in the harness story.

text: No lawsuit and no hearing record is copied: the cut-over hands over the legacy lawsuit_no and reads none of v_ace_lawsuit, v_ace_hearing or v_ace_pod, and the court record is answered by the DP07 record read of this service on its own login, key resolution staying with REC-05 and RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG.
why: Legacy AC1 forbids a copy of the court record, the three views are Section B and absent until RWB-ACE-001 lands, and the criterion itself belongs to the integration story.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC1; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.3 views 22 to 24; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP07; ADR-010; DL43
impact: A wrong reading would copy an ACE court row, which the boundary rule forbids, or block a wave 4 cut-over on a view that is not yet granted.

text: The feature switch is rwb.source-data.dm007-cutover from the platform flag library and it defaults off: off, the step refuses to start and no package leaves, and this story's version still applies because it creates nothing. The ten day evidence is read through API-P1-003 GET /admin/reconciliation/results as TSD P1 v3 states, while the tracker and data-quality-exception rows of the context pack carry no cut-over weight under D-RCV-35 U5.
why: The legacy story has no switch, the platform naming rule gives the service prefix, the context pack and TSD P1 v3 disagree on the provided operation list, and a bulk cut-over must not run before the rehearsal and the owners' loads.
read: Template and Rules §R3 default ruling Feature flags to the platform library; Template and Rules §R4 naming; context pack P1 REST operations provided; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1; D-RCV-35 U5
impact: A wrong default would let a cut-over start before the owners' loads are ready; the version creates nothing, so the schema is unaffected either way.

text: The story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded, and the release 31 December 2026 is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
why: D-RCV-60 records a missing approval as an assumption and continues in Draft without waiting, and Template and Rules §R1 U7 keeps a date unchanged, tentative and never a gap.
read: legacy RWB-DM-007 Epic E2, release 31 December 2026; D-RCV-60 overlay; Template and Rules §R1 U7
impact: The story may not be started as approved work until the status is raised; the date is not a commitment in this document.
